subject: DONE s384c (a1e3814): self-referential my-init whose comma is a list-op separator now lowers — PExpr's parse decides, not the syntactic pre-check
description:
Found by #291's family-1 deletion.  op/bless.t:69 TRANSPILE_FAILs (whole file, 106 passing rows LOST):
  Parser2 TODO: self-referential my-init with a below-assignment tail: my $c1 = bless $c1, "C3";

REPRODUCER (perl "in: C3 / out: C3"):
  $c1 = bless \(my $sv = "test"), "C";
  { my $c1 = bless $c1, "C3"; print "in: ", ref($c1), "\n"; }
  print "out: ", ref($c1), "\n";

MECHANISM.  _lower_block refuses a `my $x = <init>` when _lowprec_idx finds a depth-0 low-prec token in the init, because the whole `$x = …` run is then handed to PExpr INSIDE the let, where `$x` is the FRESH binding and not the outer variable perl reads.  In `bless $c1, "C3"` that comma is a LIST-OPERATOR argument separator, not a statement tail — PExpr parses it correctly as `(p-bless $c1 "C3")` — but the pre-check cannot tell (the `my $c = h 1, 2` ambiguity the comment cites).

The deleted `_rename_poisoned_block_mys` dodged this for free: _rename_decl_within renames the DECLARATOR but explicitly skips the decl's own RHS ("`my $x = $x` reads the OUTER $x"), so the emission became
  (let (($c1__shadow__0 (make-p-box nil))) (p-my-= $c1__shadow__0 (p-bless $c1 "C3")))
— exactly perl.  The NO-tail path already does the right thing without any rename:
  (let (($c1 (p-box-init (p-bless $c1 "C3")))))    ; init evaluates in the OUTER env

FIX OPTIONS:
 (a) Use PExpr's own answer instead of the syntactic pre-check: lower the run, and if the result is EXACTLY one assignment to $x (no comma-expression), rewrite to the no-tail shape `(let (($x (p-box-init RHS))))`.  Keeps the refusal only for a genuine `my $x = A, B`.
 (b) Targeted rename at the refusal site (rename this one declaration within its enclosing block instead of dying) — restores today's behaviour with a rule keyed on the real cause rather than on a global-name coincidence.

(a) is the better shape; (b) is the cheap one.  Guard row: the reproducer plus `my $x = $x, 1` (which must STILL be refused — parser2-02.t already asserts that).
